unit.why: A short anecdote: R. Yaakov of Sieniawa sends tobacco via the Yismah Moshe to the Seer of Lublin, who smells in it the scent of first-fruits, matching the messenger's unspoken thought.

stories.start_quote: ועובדא ידעני איש אחד חסיד ועשיר
stories.summary_en: A rich hasid of Sieniawa sends tobacco to the Seer of Lublin through the Yismah Moshe. On the way the messenger thinks that one who merely brings a gift to a scholar is like one bringing first-fruits. On smelling the tobacco the Seer says it smells of first-fruits.

quotes: והריח בו אמר שמריח ריח ביכורים
tags.why: The Seer perceives the messenger's unspoken thought through the smell.
The tobacco sent to the tzaddik is the meaningful object of the story.

quotes: המביא דורן לת"ח כאלו מביא בכורים
tags.why: Bringing a gift to a tzaddik is valued like bringing first-fruits.

quotes: ותיכף שהביאו להצדיק הק נ"ל ז"ל
tags.why: The messenger brings the gift to the tzaddik's court.

quotes: איש אחד חסיד ועשיר מק׳ שינאווע
tags.why: A wealthy hasid gives a gift to the tzaddik.
The story links a hasid, the rabbi of Sieniawa and the Seer of Lublin.

quotes: זאת העתיק לנו שארי הרה״ג ר׳ צבי יחזקאל
tags.why: The story is framed as told by the grandson of the Yismah Moshe and passed on through family tradition.
